meta.note: EFFECT ONLY. This is the case the ladder exists for: a published threshold EXISTS for this outcome, was applied by the review authors themselves, and the effect FAILED it. Most products would render this as 'reduces soreness, p = 0.0004'. Not human verified.
meta.reopened_at_source: S1 full text via Europe PMC

dose_studied: About 1 g/day combined EPA+DHA, which straddles the review's own dose split (<1000 mg/day and >1000 mg/day). Dose match is good.

sources.label: PMID 32382573 / PMC7195643
sources.title: Omega-3 PUFA supplementation for reducing muscle soreness after eccentric exercise: systematic review and meta-analysis (BioMed Research International 2020)
methods_strengths: Healthy, recreationally active participants — the population a consumer product is sold to.
Reports the magnitude on a 0–10 visual analogue scale, a unit a person can picture.
Names a published threshold and applies it to its own pooled estimate rather than leaving the reader to guess.
methods_limits: Small base: 9 studies in the soreness pool, 145 supplemented vs 156 control participants overall.
The authors rate their own evidence as low quality.

The threshold's own provenance could not be opened: it is cited to a Cochrane cold-water-immersion review, so it is domain-matched, but whether it was anchor-derived in healthy exercisers is unresolved.
sources.funding: Recorded as disclosure only, never a score penalty: no industry funder identified in the retrieved text.

outcomes.name: Muscle soreness after hard exercise
outcomes.population: Healthy, recreationally active adults, 2 days after eccentric exercise

estimate.what: delayed-onset muscle soreness 2 days after eccentric exercise, omega-3 vs placebo

also_reported.what: isometric muscle strength after eccentric exercise
also_reported.interval_note: 95% CI as reported; the interval spans no effect.

quote.text: In our current study, we used 1.4 as the minimal clinically important difference (MCID) for pain reduction based on the 10-unit VAS. It should be noticed that the effect size of less muscle soreness with n-3 PUFA was lower than the MCID, suggesting that the statistically significant difference in pain reduction was very unlikely to represent meaningful or important differences in clinical practice.

outcomes.comparator: Omega-3 versus placebo, both after the same eccentric exercise protocol.
outcomes.timeframe: Measured 2 days after the exercise bout.
outcomes.dose_applicability: Good. A consumer dose of about 1 g/day sits on the review's own dose boundary, and both the above-1000 mg and below-1000 mg subgroups were reported.

threshold.derived_in: exercise soreness literature, cited by the review to a Cochrane cold-water-immersion review; whether it was anchor-derived in healthy exercisers is unresolved
threshold.note: This is the rare outcome where a threshold exists AND was applied to this exact pooled estimate by the authors themselves. The effect is 0.93 points against a 1.4-point bar, so it is real, statistically clear, and below what was defined as mattering.

practical_importance.note: The source itself concludes the effect is below the threshold: 'does not result in a clinically important reduction of muscle soreness'. We report that verdict rather than the p-value.

limits: Low-quality evidence by the authors' own GRADE rating.
Strength and range-of-motion outcomes were null.

The threshold's derivation population could not be independently opened; it is domain-matched but its anchor basis is unresolved. Since the effect fails the bar either way, a more permissive threshold is the only thing that could change the verdict, and none was found.

not_assessed.reason: This pass graded no certainty rubric, so no certainty bar exists to show.
Triglyceride form (ethyl ester vs re-esterified) was out of scope for this effect-only test.
No dose score was computed; dose match is stated in words.

access_failures: The threshold's origin (Cochrane CD008262) could not be opened: Europe PMC returned an empty full text and the Cochrane PDF endpoint returned an HTML interstitial.
guards: A confidence interval crossing the null would mean uncertainty, not evidence of no effect.
The blood-lipid effect of omega-3 is a surrogate and is not used to support a lived claim here.
No magnitude is converted into a claim about what anyone would notice.
Funding is disclosure only and never a score penalty.
